defs_pruned: Jev is TypeSafe's hosted judge model: it answers each multiple-choice question about a text with one choice and a confidence from 0 to 1.
A Jev request is one call to it.
Recorded Jev answers are an answers file (`--answers-file`): JSON answers given to judge-jev in place of a live Jev call.
Raptor is the requirements tool that imports Markdown records into its record store and serves them to other tools (ADR-JEV-0002).
Its query interface is the way Raptor hands records to another tool.
Raptor is the requirements tool that imports Markdown records.
An issue is a diagnostic Raptor's import reports for a record, such as `UNKNOWN_SECTION`.
A record is one requirement (REQ), non-functional requirement (NFR) or architecture decision record (ADR) as Raptor imports it; REQ, NFR and ADR are its record kinds.
A location is the text judged against a record: a whole file (`path`), a Markdown section (`path#Heading`) or a code symbol (`path::Symbol`) (REQ-JEV-0207).
A mode (target mode) names what a location holds: `prompt` (prompt text), `skill` (a skill file), `task` (a task template) or `code` (source code).
A question set is the data file of questions judge-jev sends to Jev about a location for one record kind and target class.
`--profile` names a profile: a TOML file listing locations, each with its mode and the ids of the records that govern it (REQ-JEV-0204).
Jev is TypeSafe's hosted judge model: it answers each multiple-choice question about a text with one choice and a confidence from 0 to 1.
A Jev request is one call to it.
A record is one requirement (REQ), non-functional requirement (NFR) or architecture decision record (ADR) as Raptor imports it; REQ, NFR and ADR are its record kinds.
A location is the text judged against a record: a whole file (`path`), a Markdown section (`path#Heading`) or a code symbol (`path::Symbol`) (REQ-JEV-0207).
A pair is one (record, location) pair.
A stream of single requests is a sequence of Jev requests, one per pair, sent one at a time through the batch command (REQ-JEV-0002).
A record is one requirement (REQ), non-functional requirement (NFR) or architecture decision record (ADR) as Raptor imports it; REQ, NFR and ADR are its record kinds.
A question set is the data file of questions judge-jev sends to Jev about a location for one record kind and target class.
A target class is agent text (modes `prompt`, `skill` and `task`) or code (mode `code`).

A quality decision tree is the data file of questions that judges whether a record is well written: waves of questions, with rules that turn Jev's answers into the next wave or a verdict (REQ-JEV-0101).
A question-set id is the `id` field of a question set or tree file.
The content digest of a file is the SHA-256 of its bytes.
A log entry is one event a run writes through the sc-observability logger (REQ-JEV-0008).
Raptor is the requirements tool that imports Markdown records; its rules decide which text belongs to which heading.
sc-agent is the agent tool whose Rust Jev tool will replace judge-jev's Python Jev core (ADR-JEV-0007).
Tree-sitter grammars are the parsers that find a named symbol in source code.
A Jev request is one call to it.
Raptor is the requirements tool that imports Markdown records into its record store and serves them to other tools (ADR-JEV-0002).
A dry-run entry is its report of one request a live run would send.
A composed request is the full JSON body judge-jev would send to Jev.
The record's Raptor source is the Raptor index the record was read from.
A location (resolved: its path, section or symbol) is the text judged against a record: a whole file (`path`), a Markdown section (`path#Heading`) or a code symbol (`path::Symbol`) (REQ-JEV-0207).

A quality decision tree is the data file of questions that judges whether a record is well written: waves of questions, with rules that turn Jev's answers into the next wave or a verdict (REQ-JEV-0101).
A typed error is a JSON error object with a stable `code` (such as `INPUT.MALFORMED`), a `message` and a `suggested_action`.
A run name is the name every log event of one invocation carries (`--run-name`).
A definition is a term with its meaning, from a `.sc/judge-jev/*.definitions.ttl` file (ADR-JEV-0008).
It is attached to a record, or to a record and a location (the file, Markdown section or code symbol being judged).
A request's state is the data it sends to Jev next to the questions, which holds the record.
The size limit of a request is 24000 bytes.
A definition's digest is the SHA-256 of its term, text and source.
